welcome.label: Welcome · open the case

parts.label: 🗂 The case question
parts.title: The Day the Big Oak Fell
parts.body: Why did so much change when only one tree fell?

parts.label: 🧭 Your clue bar
parts.title: Find 4 clues
rows: The bar under the tabs. Tap it to see your clues.
Each game you finish fills in a clue.
Crack the case at the top of the Assignment.

welcome.script:
Hi, scientists! Welcome back to the Field Station. Today’s case starts with a tree.

[ON SCREEN: Before the oak · Before the owl]
This giant live oak stood in a Florida hammock, a shady patch of forest. A barred owl lived up in its limbs.

[ON SCREEN: After the fallen oak · After the mushrooms]
Then a storm knocked it over. Look what showed up on the trunk. Hmm. Only ONE tree fell, but the owl left, the squirrels left, and mushrooms moved in.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
That’s our case: why did so much change?

[ON SCREEN: Your clue bar]
Every game you finish adds a clue to “My clues.” Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · tie the threads (Clue 1)

parts.label: 👆 How to tie
parts.title: Drag or tap
rows: Tap a visitor to read what it does.
Drag a thread onto it, or tap the thread, then the visitor.
Tie all five, then list what you found.

warmup.script:
Let’s meet the oak’s neighbors.

(Hold up a piece of string.) Scientists draw a line, or a thread, for every connection between living things.

[ON SCREEN: The five threads]
Here are five kinds of threads. Only one is about eating!

[ON SCREEN: How to tie]
Tap a visitor to read what it does with the oak. Then drag the thread that fits, or tap the thread and then the visitor. One visitor isn’t even alive. Can you spot it?

When all five are tied, list what you found in the boxes. Press Listen. Dr. Reyes has a tip for you.

part3.label: Part 3 · pull a thread (Clue 3)

parts.label: 🔮 Predict first
parts.title: Guess, then pull
rows: Tap the living things you think will change.
Press Pull the thread and check your guess.

part3.script:
(Hold a string web or a cat’s cradle, then tug one string.) Watch. I pull one string, and look how many others move!

[ON SCREEN: The web]
This is the web around Dr. Reyes’s oak. Each colored line is one connection.

[ON SCREEN: Predict first]
Pick a thread to pull. Before you pull, predict: tap every living thing you think will change. Then press Pull the thread and see how close you were. Try all three.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie. One of these pulls surprised Dr. Reyes!

explore.label: Part 4 · the saw palmetto (Clue 4)

parts.label: 🌴 Saw palmetto
parts.title: A short palm with fan-shaped fronds
parts.body: It grows all over Florida, often right under big oaks.

explore.script:
[ON SCREEN: Saw palmetto]
Have you seen this plant? Saw palmetto grows all over Florida. Its stems have tiny teeth, like a saw. Ouch!

It’s short, but it has a web of its own.

[ON SCREEN: Five boxes]
Read about it, then drag each card into its kind of connection. One card goes in each box. That’s your last clue!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie first.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Why did so much change?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Four places to write
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

parts.label: 🛟 Help buttons
parts.title: Help under every box
rows: Chips light up as you write.
Three hints, one at a time.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You found all four clues! At the top of this tab, crack the case: why did so much change when only one tree fell?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then write your case report: two short answers, your own ecosystem web, and a CER.

[ON SCREEN: Help buttons]
Watch the chips light up as you write. Stuck? Press Hint. Your answers save as you type.

Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The quote
parts.title: Some people say…
parts.body: “As long as we have plants and animals, we don’t need to worry about the small stuff like bees, fungi, and bacteria.”

parts.label: ⚖ CER
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Claim: what you think is true.
Evidence: facts from the lesson that prove it.
Reasoning: how the facts prove your claim.

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Tap to plan
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.
They drop into your C and E boxes. You write the R.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: The quote]
Some people say, “As long as we have plants and animals, the small stuff doesn’t matter.” Bees. Mushrooms. Bacteria. Hmm. Think about the threads you pulled.

[ON SCREEN: CER]
Remember CER: your claim, your evidence from today, and your reasoning.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side, then two pieces of evidence. They drop right into your boxes. The reasoning is all you. Try starting with “This shows that…”

Press Listen. Dr. Reyes wants to hear your side.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🌰 Your specimen
parts.title: Live oak acorn
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

closing.script:
Case closed! One tree was the center of a whole web.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and a live oak acorn goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time, we’ll look at real numbers from Florida. How can you tell if a place is healthy, or out of balance?

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

part1.label: Part 1 · the real live oak (Clue 2)
part1.script:
[ON SCREEN: The live oak photo]
This is a real live oak, the same kind as Dr. Reyes’s tree. See those little ferns on the limbs? Open every number, then match each kind of connection to a number. That’s Clue 2! Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.

partc.label: Part C · your own ecosystem web
partc.script:
[ON SCREEN: Your place]
Now it’s your web. Pick a Florida place you know. Name five living things there, then three connections, each a different kind. Want to draw it? The sketch pad is a bonus.

vr.label: VR activity · Rebuild the web (separate page)

parts.label: 🧭 Two ways
parts.title: Two ways to do it
rows: VR Field Mission: build 4 connections around one big tree in Tranquil Forest.
No headset? Place 5 photo cards around the oak on your computer.

parts.label: 🥇 The badge
parts.title: Golden Acorn badge
parts.body: Save your capture in VR to earn it.

vr.script:
Hi, scientists! You cracked the case of the fallen oak. (Hold up an acorn, or make goggles with your hands.) Now let’s build it back.

[ON SCREEN: The sketch]
This is Dr. Reyes’s last sketch of the oak, from June. See the blank tags? Each one was a neighbor that needed the tree.

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]
Pick your way at the top. With a headset, go into the Tranquil Forest, pick the biggest tree, and add food, pollination, shelter and nutrient cycling around it. No headset? Place the photo cards around the oak.

[ON SCREEN: The badge]
Finish in VR and you earn the Golden Acorn badge!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.
